title: How much immunity stops an outbreak?
caption: If one case infects R₀ others in a fully susceptible population, an outbreak declines once the immune fraction is above 1 − 1/R₀, because each case then infects fewer than one other (R below 1). Measles, with R₀ of about 12–18, needs more than about 92–94% immunity, which is why very high vaccine coverage is needed.
alt: A curve of the immune fraction needed against R0, rising steeply and levelling towards 1: 0.5 at R0 of 2, 0.75 at 4, and about 0.92 to 0.94 for measles at R0 of 12 to 18.
description: The fraction immune needed to stop an outbreak is 1 − 1/R₀.
R₀ = 2: half the population must be immune.
Above that fraction each case infects fewer than one other person, so the outbreak declines.
axisLabels: R₀, new cases per case when everyone is susceptible
